data.name: UAYEB: The Dry Land
data.detailed_description:
Free Demo



The free demo is available on the 22nd of May 2017.

The demo is between 2 to 4 hours of the begining of the game.
It is like the tutorial, where you explore, look for objects to use and for helping you to solve puzzles. There is a bit of crafting, one fight with enemies and one golden Mayan artifact to find in a cave.


Acerca do jogo

This is an Indie game made by one person only, and two actors for the voices.

UAYEB: The Dry Land - Episode 1 is a solo story driven adventure / survival / crafting / puzzle game, placed in an open world of 16km2, with the immersive First Person view.
- Craft your equipment and go treasure hunt to find 20 Mayans artifacts.
- Each artifact in located in a different level with traps and puzzles.
- The gameplay ingredients are integrated in a linear story, with a increase of difficulty throughout the levels.
- It takes around 30 to 40 hours to finish the game.

Game details:
This is not a survival sandbox game. The survival parts are used to add variety and difficulty to the adventure.

You as Uayeb, will explore and survive in a hostile environment, you will find clues helped by your friend archeologist Joanna, to discover Mayan artifacts that will lead you to the lost civilization, you will craft your equipment to be ready for the adventure.

SOLVE PUZZLES:
Nothing in UAYEB will be shown with a big arrow.
You will have to think by yourself to know where to go, and to solve puzzles you'll be helped by Joanna's clues that she will put somewhere in the world.

SURVIVE:
Drink, eat, sleep, cold and hot places, stamina, heal, batteries, weapons and ammunition.
Avoid deadly traps, stay alive in underwater caves, jump on moving Mayan platforms, don't touch swords traps that arise from ground.

EXPLORE:
Explore a vast world with desert and dune sand, forests and water falls, beaches and a lost city, and find clues that will lead you to Mayan artifacts.

CRAFTING:
Find blueprints and collect resources to build up your own equipment.

FIGHT:
Defend yourself against hostile survivors with three different fire weapons and melee moves.

ARTIFACTS:
There will be a lot of Mayan artifacts to find for finishing the first episode. Each artifact will be a level specific with traps, platforms, puzzles and enemies.
You will need to find clues to be able to reach the artifacts.

To find the Mayans artifacts you will encounter moving platforms, unstable parts or planks, swords traps, balls with spikes falling, other deadly mechanisms, sulfur sprays that will project you in the air and few more surprises!

Time in game:
Like the real world, the time in Uayeb will turn around 24 hours.
1 hour in real life is like around 2h30 in game.
You can sleep at any time (if you have a bed), to rest and pass the time faster.

Length:
To finish the Episode 1 and find the 20 Golden Mayan artifacts, it takes around 30 to 40 hours depending of you skills.


There are also music bonuses to find and easter eggs of games and films references.

reviews.review:
UAYEB. Have you heard about it? No? Well, me neither until I got it in a pack of games from Humble Bundle and decided to give it a try. After many fruitful experiences and spent 35h later I can give some answers what it is about.

+The world is wide and beautiful (I approve CryEngine)
+Long lifetime (30-40h)
+Nice mixture of puzzles, platforming and first person shooting
+Cool story
+Numerous resources to collect and things to craft
+Quite unique experience all the way

-The world feels empty 
-Crude enemy AI which seems to be blind, but then when facing you it detects you through the thickest of bushes
-Some nasty occasional bugs
-Stiff first few hours
-When voice acting is not bad it's amusing

UAYEB is a survival game based in a post-apocalyptic world in near future where Mayan indians actually foresaw it correctly that world ends in 2012, but the way things happened were slower than originally was presumed. Whatsoever you play a guy called Uayeb - one of the few survivors in the world where only friendly contact seems to be a woman named Joanna.

The game begins when protogonist wakes up from freezing chamber where he has spent more than a short while and has lost his memory. I could immediately feel first person puzzle game elements strong and reminding me of games like Myst and new Tesla Effect while wondering inside the large apartment and hunting items. Things change however after you step out of the house you woke up. 16 square kilometer area is free to be explored technically without limits, but there is not much point in it at the beginning at least because you must take care of thirst and hunger and you can't go wondering in the desert before you have proper supplies and a map.

Being developed with CryEngine, especially the nature look astonishing and with the successful landscape designs the look of the game really pleases an eye. Excluding my graphic card my current computer is not brand new and it still could deal the game without bigger lags.

First few hours of the game can be frustrating, even painful for minimal supplies, resources and not much clue what do to. You might feel pushed in the deeper and colder end of the pool, but when you get the hang of it - it begins to go better and better. Joanna will reward you with useful assets like map and blueprints to craft things like solar panels, bandages and even a car powered by sunlight. To craft things you will need materials which also becomes easier when you find right places because every material (excluding very rare gold) spawns back after a moment. (Also it is good thing to note that when I played, in the beginning there were no quick saves, amounts of resources were tinier. Moreover the hunger and thirst became more quickly)

The main point and sugar or should I say gold of the game is 20 Mayan artifacts which each lie in different places in the world and each one is an unique scenario where you need to use your head and equipment to leave the trophy in your hands and in one piece. Some of them can be very tricky because usually clues do not enlighten things a lot, but still it never did feel unfair. Indiana Jones movies seem to have improvised the game a lot. As long as you got enough drink and food supplies and travel during daytime it helps a lot already. The storytelling walks hand in hand with the artifact hunting and while there is not any face to face conversation the audio tracks which Joanna sends are interesting to listen when the identity of the protogonist is revealed bit by bit.

It goes without saying that I liked UAYEB a lot, but I still wouldn't say it was a GOTY material. There is very much cool things, but also several shortages. Usually when we are talking about open world games there should also be the point or motive actually go in places. For example in recent Far Cry games you can find yourself on the top of the mountain looking in a horizon and seeing some ancient construction. After that you take your vehicle and travel to that place and during trip you see a lot of other points of interests which can be side missions etc. Of course the artifacts are sprinkled in different places of the map, but you can't access the sites until you have collected the related clue which again can be only collected only in certain order. So UAYEB's huge, but lifeless world can feel a bit dull for the lack of NPCs and wild animals and in its worst the game can feel a fan mod for some larger game. It is necessary to note however that the game is an indie game produced by one developer with the limited budget. And while I don't want to praise the game too much for being developed by only two hands, I say that this guy seems to listen customers and answers swiftly and politely for sent feedback.

I would have recommended the game to be purchased when in sale, but after recent updates and cut of price I say that the price tag is totally reasonable. There is also a free demo available! I hope to see the travels of Uayeb continue in a future in promised Episode 2.
